To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neural networks with 3D convolutional and residual architectures are capable of achieving a 99% accuracy in discriminating neutrinoless double beta decay signal from the background events in the high-pressure gased TPC detector.

3D neural networks are more powerful than their 2D counterparts, the 3D networks are more robust against different experimental conditions, and the residual network structure is a promising approach for signal/background discrimination in TPC-based double-beta decay experiments.
the neural network methods we used are capable of discriminating signal events from background events in high-pressure gasses with high accuracy.

these methods are promising for future applications in high pressure gas TPC detectors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neural networks have already harnassed a large portion of the discrimination power that the three-dimensional charge information of the TPC can provide, and the methods can be further improved by increasing the depth of the network and/or by using more advanced network architectures.
3D CNN models are a promising approach for the discrimination between signal and background events in neutrinoless double beta decay searches.
the 3D neural networks can be used as a powerful tool for signal/background separation in high-pressure gasses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3D convolutional networks are capable of capturing the spatial information of tracks and the residual networks are able to learn and improve on the features of the tracks in a way that the 3DCNNs cannot.
the 3D information of charge tracks in the TPC is a very powerful handle to discriminate the neutrinoless double beta decay signal from backgrounds.
the neural network models, when trained on the full charge distribution of the ionization charge track, can learn and extract the subtle difference between signal and background events.
